Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given the competitor's aggressive entry pricing, but that memory only measured activation/revenue lift over 12 billing periods and said nothing about retention quality, cohort price-sensitivity, or long-term margin erosion — a reactive discount could win short-term share while degrading the 'qualified' part of the revenue objective, so I want to verify its original record before ever considering it, even though I'm not choosing it this week. I'm also verifying memory_86 since it's the closer analog to the current onboarding completion drop and I want to confirm effect size and sample quality before committing the only experiment slot this week. Simplify_onboarding is lower-risk, addresses two of the three live problems simultaneously, and doesn't gamble on price-based competitive response before we understand its downstream revenue-quality effects. I'm running it as a standard (not broad) experiment given ongoing uncertainty about interaction with the competitive pricing pressure, and flagging that the pricing question remains open and should be the next verified experiment.
